# Experience First

Choose the user's experience when it conflicts with implementation convenience.

- Justify every feature, control, and option.
- Prefer a polished experience with three features to a rough experience with ten.
- Prototype design decisions before committing to them. A disposable HTML prototype costs less than a change to production code.
- Refine transitions, alignment, spacing, feedback, and error states.
- Tighten the core loop. Every feature should serve the central workflow or stay out of its way.

The user is whoever consumes the work.
For a UI, that is the end user.
For a library or internal API, it is the colleague who imports it.
The next engineer who maintains the code is also a user.
Give their experience the same weight.
Explain the impact from their perspective.

Foundations should serve the experience.
[Foundational Thinking](foundational-thinking.md) governs the sequence of work.
This principle governs its target.
